implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosures are gating documents in hostile or third-party acquisitions; the timing and content of this filing will determine whether an open offer obligation is triggered and the acquirer's identity, holding structure, and funding source become public.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement when substantial acquisition (typically ≥5% voting share) occurs; must be filed within two trading days.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Code — Regulation 3 (definition of 'person' and 'group')
framework.note: Determines whether acquirer acts alone or as part of a group; affects disclosure scope and open offer thresholds.
May apply to acquisitions by promoters, inter-group transfers, or statutory acquisitions; exemptions must be declared in the disclosure.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Code — Regulation 10 (Open Offer obligation)
framework.note: Acquisition of ≥25% triggers mandatory open offer to all shareholders at specified price. Disclosure under Reg 31(4) often precedes open offer announcement.
Post-acquisition, acquirer shareholding may trigger consolidated reporting and related-party disclosure under IND-AS and MCA rules.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 30 (Disclosure of Material Events)
framework.note: Company must simultaneously make a disclosure to stock exchanges under Regulation 30 when informed of substantial acquisition.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 — Sections 48, 56 (capital gains on share transfer)
framework.note: Acquirer's tax liability on share purchase; seller's capital gains tax if applicable.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) — if acquirer is foreign
framework.note: Foreign direct investment must comply with FDI policy and RBI Press Notes; sector-specific caps and approval may apply.

headline: Quintegra Solutions Limited: Substantial Acquisition Disclosure filed under SEBI Takeover Code
sum: Quintegra Solutions Limited has filed a mandatory disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulation 31(4) relating to a substantial acquisition of shares. The disclosure indicates a transaction triggering the 5% threshold under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
detail: Under SEBI Regulation 31(4), when a person or group acquires 5% or more of the voting capital of a listed company (or crosses specified thresholds), a disclosure must be made to the stock exchange and the company within two trading days. This filing by Quintegra Solutions Limited signals that a material change in shareholding has occurred or is in progress. The precise identity of the acquirer, the number of shares acquired, the acquisition price, and conditions precedent are contained in the filed disclosure document.
